# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 7 | **Condition:** Better preserved

---

**7:1** I thank You, O Lord, for You have made me a source of running streams in a dry land, a water spring in a desert.

**7:2** And irrigation for a garden [...] a pool fed by a living spring.

**7:3** And You have planted cypresses and elms alongside cedars, all for Your glory.

**7:4** Trees of life beside a hidden spring, tucked away among all the waterside trees.

**7:5** They will send out a shoot to become an everlasting grove, putting down roots before they ever bloom.

**7:6** And they will push their roots all the way to the underground stream and their trunk will open up to the living water.

**7:7** And it will become a never-ending fountain. And on its leafy branches all the forest animals will feed.

**7:8** And its base will be walked over by every traveler, and birds will perch on its branches.

**7:9** And all the waterside trees will tower over it, because they shoot up tall where they are planted.

**7:10** But they never send their roots down to the deep water source.

**7:11** And the shoot of the sacred planting, the planting of truth, stays hidden and overlooked, and the secret of its seal remains unknown.

**7:12** And You, O God, have protected its fruit with the secret force of mighty warriors and holy spirits.

**7:13** And the swirling sword of flame, so that no outsider can reach the fountain of life.

**7:14** Or drink the holy waters alongside the eternal trees.

**7:15** Or bear fruit with the planting of the clouds, because such a one sees but does not understand.

**7:16** And thinks it over but cannot trust the source of life. And so that one puts forth a bud toward [...] the eternal fountain.

**7:17** And I have become something the flooding rivers mock, because they splash their mud all over me.

**7:18** But You, my God, placed in my mouth the first rains for all [...] and a spring of water that gives life.

**7:19** And it will never run dry, opening the skies without stopping. And the waters will become a flood, overflowing.

**7:20** Into oceans without shore [...] and they will erupt without warning from their hiding place, and they will become [...] torrents of water.

**7:21** For all this was invisible to every eye [...] and kept from human knowledge.

**7:22** And Israel dismissed them as worthless [...] among the ordinary waterside trees.

**7:23** But the fruit-bearing tree [...] will put out its branch to become an everlasting planting.

**7:24** And it will root itself in all the earth, and through its branches all [...] the waterside trees.

**7:25** And they will spread their roots into the parched ground and [...] waters will flow.

**7:26** For it is a truth-planting that produces branches of holiness for an everlasting grove.

**7:27** And all the rivers of Eden will water its sacred boughs.

**7:28** And it will grow into a towering tree with sweeping branches, and every creature of the field will find shelter under it.

**7:29** And its shade will blanket the whole world, and its crown will brush the clouds.

**7:30** And its roots will plunge down into the abyss.

**7:31** They will put forth a shoot for an everlasting planting, rooting deep before they bloom.

**7:32** And they will drive their roots toward the underground stream.

**7:33** And the spring will be unsealed for a blessed planting, an eternal water source.

**7:34** And every forest creature will feed on its leafy branches.

**7:35** And its base will be walked on by every passerby, and its limbs will hold up every bird.

**7:36** And none of the waterside trees will ever overpower it, because its roots reach all the way to the deep water source.

**7:37** And it produces its fruit right on time and its leaves never wither.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 7 is pure poetry — a vision of cosmic renewal through a single, secret planting. The Eden imagery is deliberate: God guards the fountain of life with a "whirling flame" (the cherubim of Genesis 3:24). The climax — a world-tree whose shade covers the earth — is breathtaking eschatological hope.*
